extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing or advising on USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing an affidavit of resignation/consent-to-exclusion submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the related disciplinary findings, publication, and reinstatement presumptions before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is determined by the Director of the USPTO upon review; the Final Order here states the affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' The affidavit should include the specific acknowledgments and consents described in the Order (see related criteria below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent (no coercion or duress)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that the respondent's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and that the respondent is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact wording in the affidavit: 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.' This establishes voluntariness of the resignation/consent-to-exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending OED investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the respondent is aware the OED Director opened an investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 into allegations that the respondent violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the affidavit's acknowledgment of the specific OED file and that the investigation 'delved into and obtained information' (here, regarding a guilty plea). The affidavit should identify the subject matter of the investigation sufficiently to show the respondent's awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of OED opinion of specific rule violation (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that the OED Director is of the opinion, based on the investigation, that the respondent violated a specified provision of the USPTO Rules (the Order cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order quotes the alleged rule: 'It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a practitioner in other respects.' The affidavit should state the respondent's awareness of the OED's opinion identifying the particular rule(s) at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that, if and when the respondent applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of the reinstatement application, that (a) the facts regarding the respondent in the OED file are true, and (b) the respondent could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations embodied in the OED Director's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit's acknowledgment is binding for limited purposes of evaluating any future reinstatement application; the Order reproduces the two presumption points (a) and (b) verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of relevant regulations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the respondent has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses that the respondent knowingly accepts the procedural and substantive consequences of exclusion and of the admitted presumptions for reinstatement; the affidavit should identify the cited regulations by section number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit consent to exclusion from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must include an explicit statement that the respondent consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order records the simple affirmative: 'He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.' This is the operative surrender of practice rights under the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory and regulatory authority to approve and exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has authority under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order affirms this authority as the basis for approving the affidavit and ordering exclusion; submissions should be made with awareness that approval is an act of the Director under cited statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b), it is professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner in other respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order applies this provision to the facts investigated (here, a guilty plea for Possession of Child Pornography); allegations of criminal conduct that bear on honesty/trustworthiness can support OED opinions of rule violations leading to discipline or consented exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements for exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with a provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template notice should include: the respondent's name and registration number; that the affidavit was accepted and the respondent was excluded on consent; that the affidavit was submitted while an investigation was pending and the subject matter of that investigation; that the OED Director was of the opinion of a specific rule violation; the reinstatement presumptions; the statutory/regulatory authority; and the FOIA reading room link. The Order directs electronic posting and Official Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties and restrictions on excluded practitioners) and must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically commands full compliance with these sections; practitioners and counsel should consult those sections for the detailed duties (e.g., notification, handling of client matters) and the reinstatement process requirements.
